newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end up but off highs, seen weakening.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end up but off highs, seen weakening.

text.p: FCOJ futures ended firmer for the third consecutive session, lifted by speculative short-covering and options-related trade, market sources said.
"Some weak spec shorts are covering but overall (the market) is going nowhere," Celeste Georgakis, vice president with Dean Witter, said.
Indeed, trade selling knocked prices off the highs near the close. Georgakis said trade scale-up selling could cap gains around 80.00 cents in March.
Forecasts for mild weather across the Florida citrus belt for the remainder of the week will add some fundamental pressure on the market.
March frozen concentrated orange juice settled 0.20 cent firmer at 78.70 cents per pound, traded 79.70 to 78.50 cents. May went out 0.25 cent higher at 81.60 cents.
Volume was estimated at 4,000 lots compared with Friday's official volume of 5,757 lots.
Analysts put longer-term resistance at 84.00 cents in March and at 87.00 cents in May.
